The most popular class Cyrus has taught is called Avoiding AI, which explains what Generative AI is, some of the concerns around it, and how to disable it and find alternatives. The first time she taught the class in fall of 2025 more than 70 people enrolled.

caption:
Hannah Cyrus is a librarian in Bangor, Maine. Patrons kept coming to her with the same question: how do I turn this stuff off. So she built a class called Avoiding AI. Her Intro to Computers class usually gets about a dozen people. She capped registration at 30, opened a waitlist, put it on Zoom, and about 70 attended each of the first two.

Charlie Bailey ran the same class in South Philadelphia after reading what she wrote about hers. The library's Instagram post about it got over 2,000 likes and 220 shares, where most of that library's posts do not clear a few dozen. He scheduled a second session because the first overfilled. Dozens of librarians around the world have emailed Cyrus asking for her materials, and 20 Maine librarians enrolled to take the class from her this spring.

The caveat is worth stating plainly. This is not a rejection of computers. Cyrus is the one who points out how useful optical character recognition is for scanning old documents at the library. The argument is about who chose the setting.

slides.title: One hour, phones out
slides.body: Charlie Bailey runs the same class in South Philadelphia. He puts the steps on a projector and walks the room through *turning the features off*, one platform at a time. Nobody is asked to give anything up. They are shown where the setting lives.
slides.evidence: Then, he walks through all of the most popular tech platforms and devices, showing step-by-step instructions on the projector to guide people through turning off specific features.

slides.caveat: Cyrus is the one who points out how useful the software that scans old library documents is. What she wants back is the choice.
slides.evidence: Cyrus mentioned how useful optical character recognition is for scanning old documents at the library. But for her and the people who go to her workshops, the anti-AI movement isn’t about rejecting technology altogether so much as it is about advocating for more control, agency, and freedom in how people use technology.

slides.title: A town library made it a service
slides.body: In Searsmont, Maine, the town library will now sit with you and *take the AI off your phone*. Its director switches off assistants like Siri, and moves people to a search engine that still answers without a summary bolted on top.
slides.evidence: Brown helps patrons disable AI-powered assistants like Siri or so-called smart features in email and switch from using Google, which doesn’t offer an option to search without AI overviews, to a browser that does.
